chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: The Casino de Paris as a theater restaurant
summary: Jackson locates and describes the theater restaurant, its convertible stage, floor show with Cardini and Smith and Dale, and Max Baer replaced by Bojangles.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now this was Casino de Paris on -- ?
On 54th -- between 54th and 53rd Street. Let me see, --
On what -- What avenue was that?
No, it was on Broadway, between Broadway and Eighth Avenue.
Oh, between Broadway and Eighth Avenue.
Yeah, but the club extended from 54th to 53rd Street, you see.
I see.
You understand?
Sure.
It took up that block, in other words.
Oh, yes.
And it was a theater restaurant, and on the stage you would do the show.
That would be like where the Ed Sullivan Theater is now, right?
No, no, no.
That's 53rd and 54th.
Yeah, but the theater is more near Eighth Avenue to what I'm talking about.
Near Eighth Avenue. Oh, yes, the CBS Theater.
That's right.
I'm trying to pinpoint it down. I see.
That's right. That's right. And then, after the show, they would turn the panels around and make a big chrome semicircle and the people would go up there and dance on the same stage.
Oh, that's interesting.
Uh-huh. It had a beautiful show. It had Cardini in there, [Houdini Hindu] Smith and Dale. It
had a chorus line of 24 girls and it had 16 showgirls. And Max Baer, he opened it.
Oh, is that so?

That's right, and Max Baer, he wanted to be a playboy and so one night he didn't show up for the show and he was out with the girls, so Billy Rose fired him and that's when he got Bill Bojangles Robinson to come and take his place.
Wow.
Yeah.
